_note: Validation fixtures for the per-Story TEST_CASE prompt (T2). Deliberately spans distinct domains (clinical / fintech / logistics) plus three behaviour probes (trivial=boundedness, no_acs=loud inference, rich=coverage-at-scale + the maxItems ceiling). Each story carries the full §8 contract (siblingNames + sharedAcceptanceCriteria + specSummary) so the harness exercises informational completeness, not a starved call. ACs are written with deliberate numeric boundaries and implied negative paths so falsifiability + edge/negative coverage can be judged rule-by-rule across runs.

story.name: Record a medication administration
story.user_story: As a ward nurse, I want to record that I gave a patient a medication dose, so that the medication-administration record is accurate and the next nurse can see what was given.
story.description: Nurse scans the patient wristband and the medication, enters the dose, and confirms administration. The system records it against the active prescription.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A dose may only be recorded against an active prescription for that patient.
AC2: The recorded dose must be within the prescribed minimum and maximum for that prescription; a dose outside the range is blocked.
AC3: For a high-alert medication, a second nurse must co-sign within 5 minutes or the administration is not committed.
AC4: Each recorded administration stores the administering nurse, the timestamp, and the dose.

sharedAcceptanceCriteria: Every clinical action is written to an immutable audit log.
A user may only act on patients in a ward they are assigned to.
stories.specSummary: Inpatient electronic medication management: prescribing, administration with barcode verification, high-alert co-signing, and discharge reconciliation.

story.name: Transfer funds between own accounts
story.user_story: As a retail banking customer, I want to move money between my own accounts, so that I can manage my balances instantly.
story.description: Customer picks a source and destination account they own, enters an amount, and confirms. The transfer settles immediately.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The transfer is rejected if the amount exceeds the available balance of the source account.
AC2: A single transfer may not exceed 25,000 in the account currency.
AC3: The total transferred from one account in a calendar day may not exceed 50,000.
AC4: Source and destination must be different accounts both owned by the customer.
AC5: On success, both account balances reflect the transfer immediately and a reference number is returned.

sharedAcceptanceCriteria: All monetary amounts are handled to two decimal places with no rounding loss.
Every money movement is reversible only via an explicit reversal transaction, never by edit.
stories.specSummary: Retail banking money-movement module: internal transfers, external payees, standing orders, with per-transaction and daily limits.

story.name: Assign a parcel to a delivery van
story.user_story: As a depot dispatcher, I want to assign a parcel to a van on a route, so that it is delivered within its promised window.
story.description: Dispatcher selects a parcel and a van scheduled for a route; the system validates fit and adds the parcel to the van's manifest.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A parcel may only be assigned to a van whose remaining weight capacity is at least the parcel's weight.
AC2: A parcel may only be assigned to a van whose route covers the parcel's destination postcode.
AC3: The parcel's promised delivery window must fall within the van's route operating hours.
AC4: A parcel that is already on a manifest cannot be assigned to a second van.

siblingNames: Assign a parcel to a delivery van
sharedAcceptanceCriteria: A parcel's chain of custody is recorded at every handover.
Capacity figures are read from the van's current load, never a cached value.
stories.specSummary: Last-mile delivery operations: route planning, parcel-to-van assignment with capacity and service-area checks, live re-routing, and proof of delivery.

stories.probe: boundedness — must NOT pad a trivial story

story.name: Show the application version in the footer
story.user_story: As any user, I want to see the application version in the page footer, so that I can quote it when reporting an issue.
story.description: The footer displays the current build version string.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The footer shows the current application version string on every page.

siblingNames: Show the application version in the footer
sharedAcceptanceCriteria: All pages share one footer component.
stories.specSummary: Global chrome for the web app: navigation, footer, cookie consent.

story.name: Export the report
story.user_story: As an analyst, I want to export the report I am viewing, so that I can share it outside the tool.
story.description: An export action on the report view produces a downloadable file.

sharedAcceptanceCriteria: Exported files never include data the requesting user is not entitled to see.
stories.specSummary: Reporting module: interactive reports with filtering, export, and scheduled email delivery.

story.name: Schedule a recurring payment
story.user_story: As a customer, I want to schedule a recurring payment to a payee, so that a fixed amount is paid automatically on a regular cadence.
story.description: Customer chooses a payee, an amount, a frequency, a start date, and an optional end date; the system runs the payment on each due date.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A recurring payment requires a payee, an amount greater than zero, a frequency (weekly or monthly), and a start date not in the past.
AC2: If an end date is given, it must be on or after the start date.
AC3: On a due date with insufficient funds, the payment is skipped, the customer is notified, and the schedule continues to the next due date.
AC4: A monthly payment whose start day exceeds the days in a given month runs on that month's last day.
AC5: The customer may cancel a recurring payment at any time; no payment runs on or after the cancellation.
AC6: Each run records the run date, amount, and outcome (paid or skipped).

sharedAcceptanceCriteria: All money movements post to the ledger exactly once (no double-charge on retry).
Every monetary amount is handled to two decimal places.
stories.specSummary: Retail banking payments: one-off payee payments, internal transfers, and recurring payment schedules with retry and cancellation.
